lede: Election night hit five feeds at once: Polymarket, Wikipedia, Lemmy, Bluesky and Mastodon all turned to the 2026 midterms, and the House market alone moved $11M in 24 hours while parked at 100 percent yes. The strangest number of the day sits on Wikipedia, where a man named Jesús de Miguel drew 585,060 views, about a third more than the election article itself, on a day nothing else in the feeds explains. A magnitude 5.4 quake struck near Rioblanco, Colombia.

throughlines.title: Will the Democratic Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
throughlines.gist: Hacker News is running live midterm coverage that calls Senate control for the Democrats, and Polymarket has settled the same question at 100 percent, on $7.6M of volume in a day.

throughlines.title: Will the Democrats win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
throughlines.gist: Lemmy is calling a historic Texas flip as James Talarico turns the state blue, and the Polymarket Texas Senate market backs it at 100 percent on nearly $5M traded in 24 hours.

throughlines.title: mary peltola
throughlines.gist: Mary Peltola is breaking out on Google Trends as her Alaska Senate race stays live on Polymarket, where she leads at 97 percent, the one contest the day's markets have not yet called outright.
